pickupCauses: The controller applied Action rules and crate cooldown visibility before world.updateVisibility. Its distance-culling pass then overwrote crate.mesh.visible, showing AI-consumed/cooldown crates and Classic crates that collection correctly rejected.
Collection sampled only the vehicle centre at the end of a physics step. Fast grazing crossings of the existing 2.4 metre circle could fall entirely between samples.
pickupFixes: A final logical availability gate now runs after the distance pass. Hidden cooldown or Classic crates cannot reappear as collectable props.

The browser and course-race checks share collectPickup, which sweeps a bounded actual movement segment through the existing pickup circle. Large reset paths and remote/finished vehicles cannot collect.
Inventory capacity, 3 second inventory cooldown, 5 second crate respawn, and existing gadget effects are preserved.
touchCauses: Pressed screen halves painted an animated red gradient over the racing canvas.
Generic button click feedback also targeted steering controls; native mobile tap highlighting remained enabled.
Unchanged pointer moves and repeated key presses rewrote feedback state, including a transient release/re-hold on repeated keys.
touchFixes: Steering feedback is confined to small direction labels. Screen halves remain transparent in active, hover, clicked and held states, with native tap highlight disabled.
Steering and continuous pedal controls are excluded from generic menu click feedback.
Unchanged held direction produces no repeated CSS/ARIA changes, and repeated keys retain the original pointer owner.

newAssertions: Classic crate meshes remain hidden after distance pass
spent crate remains hidden after render
tests/interactions.mjs.scope: Production controller and physics executed in a DOM/renderer test harness. Renderer is mocked; no browser/device FPS claim.

tests/course-races.mjs.scope: All three routes, six actual drivers, Classic and Action, shared pickup logic, item/oil use, and presentation-rate equivalence.

limitations: Mobile visual flicker fix requires the root browser/device verification pass; CPU regressions do not measure mobile compositing or 3D FPS.
